ancestry.non_overlap: GWT/runtime/coupling findings were explicitly dropped after a live crossread showed a concurrent worker had already published that shard. This receipt covers only language/tool representation, parser/repair, context-efficiency and ClayCode-precursor history.

findings.claim: Project-Frankenstein's agentic tool layer defines typed tool metadata and JSON-Schema parameters and instructs the model to emit a JSON object with action plus action_input; risk level and approval requirements remain host-side metadata rather than model authority.
findings.implication: ClayCode should preserve typed arguments and external effect/approval authority while replacing JSON surface verbosity with a canonical semantic IR plus reader-specific projections where evidence supports it.

findings.claim: Early agentic execution repeatedly required JSON-format reminders, duplicate-tool-call detection, higher parse-failure tolerance and model routing chosen specifically for JSON reliability. This shows that generic JSON correctness was a material small-model orchestration cost rather than a free interface property.
findings.next_test: Benchmark current Qwen-class readers on canonical ClayCode projections versus JSON and key/value baselines for parse success, repair turns, token cost and semantic preservation.

findings.claim: The direct Frank tool path later uses a LoRA-learned compact <tool>name|param1|param2</tool> wire format, dynamically generates the available-tool prompt, and parses primarily with string operations; however the same parser retains multiple hybrid/square-bracket fallbacks, alias repair and fuzzy matching for recurrent model misformats.
findings.implication: This is a strong historical precursor to ClayCode's machine-oriented compact representation, but it is not yet a semantic IR: syntax repair and fuzzy aliases demonstrate that surface compactness alone does not provide canonical identity.

findings.claim: The March Deep-Agents integration filtered 44 tools down to at most 15 task-relevant tools, offloaded tool results above about 1500 characters to a scratchpad, and added plan recitation to keep a 3B model on task. Later project context compaction reduced old tool/text blocks once estimated context exceeded about 40K tokens.
findings.implication: Small-model reliability depended on selective projection and externalized state, supporting ClayCode/ClayGraph designs where canonical semantics are rich but each reader receives only the relevant bounded projection.

findings.claim: At the frozen head, Project-Frankenstein contains two materially different tool-call dialects: JSON action/action_input in the agentic registry and compact pipe-delimited <tool> tags in the direct Frank registry. A compatibility parser bridges some paths, but the semantic identity of a call is not defined by one shared canonical representation.
findings.implication: ClayCode should explicitly separate canonical semantic identity from wire syntax and canonicalize equivalent reader projections before effect validation/execution.

findings.claim: V15 and later fixes had to strip leaked <tool> markup from user-visible text, cap stray tool calls and strip an additional pipe-delimited tool-tag variant. Tool syntax therefore leaked across presentation/execution boundaries in real historical operation.
findings.implication: Model-emitted representation must never itself confer execution authority; parser, validator, capability gateway, commit/effect gateway and presentation renderer require explicit typed boundaries and adversarial regression tests.

findings.claim: IAPT_METHOD.md reports that regex-based output filtering acted as an invisible co-author of model language and that replacing those filters with structured tool tags improved observed authenticity. The same report records tool-selection accuracy increasing from 45% to 78% across seven training iterations, but these measurements are project-authored and not independent replication.
findings.next_test: Re-run format/parser ablations with fixed model checkpoints and blinded scoring, separating training effects from parser effects and measuring exact format adherence plus task success.

findings.claim: Historical FRANK repeatedly changed output/token budgets and model/tool context to manage latency and small-model reliability; the February architecture benchmark also recorded reasoning timeouts caused by router/workspace overhead despite identical underlying model weights. This directly establishes context/interface overhead as a first-class system cost.
findings.implication: ClayCode evaluation must score semantic correctness together with context tokens, repair turns, latency and downstream effect success; compactness without preserved semantics or lower total repair cost is not progress.

architecture_lineage: regex/natural-language routing and JSON agent actions
-> explicit typed tool registry + JSON Schema
-> selective tool/context projection and scratch offload
-> current ClayCode target: canonical semantic IR + deterministic canonicalization + reader projections + external capability/effect authority

branch_feedback.claycode: Treat the Project-Frankenstein compact tool-tag language as a historical precursor, not as the target language. Preserve typed arguments, deterministic semantic identity and external authority; test JSON/key-value/tag/ClayCode projections against parse, repair, token and semantic-preservation baselines.
branch_feedback.frank: Do not reintroduce multiple semantic tool dialects. Needle/external deterministic machinery should translate human/model surface forms into one Clay semantic representation before capability/effect validation.
branch_feedback.harness: Add regression fixtures for malformed JSON, hybrid tags, square-bracket tags, alias/fuzzy repair, duplicate calls, leaked tool markup, overlong tool results, context compaction and semantic-equivalence canonicalization.
branch_feedback.claygraph: Historical task-selective tool projection supports bounded reader-specific views over a richer canonical substrate; reader omission must not mutate truth/provenance.
branch_feedback.unifieddb: The dual-dialect history is evidence for one semantic identity across multiple physical/wire representations, not for forcing all stores or readers into one syntax.
branch_feedback.clay: Carry forward selective projection and compact state transport, but score total repair/effect cost rather than surface token count alone.

earned_work_candidates.mechanism_or_result: Typed tool schema + compact LoRA tool projection + known repair/failure corpus provide direct parser/canonicalizer/harness design inheritance.
earned_work_candidates.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: ClayCode baseline benchmark must demonstrate that these inherited tests/design constraints actually reduce implementation/search effort or prevent regressions.

earned_work_candidates.mechanism_or_result: Historical selective tool projection, scratch offload and context compaction establish implemented patterns for bounded small-model context.
earned_work_candidates.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: Current 4B reader benchmarks must show task-equivalent or better performance under bounded projection versus full-context baseline.

earned_work_candidates.mechanism_or_result: JSON parse failures, tool-tag misformats, output-tag leaks and duplicate call history form an executable negative-regression corpus.
earned_work_candidates.falsifier_or_validation_receipt: Harness must reproduce representative historical failures against compatibility projections and prove current gateway prevents unauthorized/leaked effects.
